title: Tigers’ Justin Verlander targeting one final home start at Comerica Park
content:
If health permits, then Justin Verlander will make one final start to bookend his illustrious 21-year career on Saturday, Sept. 26 at Comerica Park.

The Detroit Tigers had already planned to dedicate the final weekend of the regular season to celebrating Verlander through a series of giveaways and in-stadium events. Now, Verlander might be able to take part in the celebration in the only way he knows how — by toeing the slab for what would be the 557th regular-season start of his career.

“It would have been real easy to give up, but that’s not what got me to this point in my career,” Verlander said. “That’s not who I am. So a month or so ago, when it started feeling a little bit better, there was a glimmering hope, a chance in my head that I could get back out there. We’re getting very close to that being reality.”

After signing a one-year, $13 million deal over the offseason, 2026 was meant to represent a homecoming for the 43-year-old, a chance to return to the franchise where it all began. However, after just one start, things quickly fell apart.

Verlander, who made his season debut on the road against the Arizona Diamondbacks, lasted all of 3 2/3 innings. That was March 30. By April 4, he’d been placed on the 15-day IL with left hip inflammation, an ailment that later required a move to the 60-day IL in May.

Since then, it’s been setback after setback for the three-time Cy Young Award winner, his chances of adding to his historic career, and then his chances of even making one last start, slowly fading away.

In July, Verlander announced his intentions to retire at the end of the season. At the same time, MLB commissioner Rob Manfred named Verlander a “Legend Pick” for the 2026 All-Star Game, his 10th selection and an opportunity to connect with the future of baseball.

Though Verlander did not pitch at the Midsummer Classic, he nevertheless persisted in his rehab, his efforts opening the door for a final start.

To get to Sept. 26, Verlander will need to make it through a few more bullpen sessions, then a simulated game next weekend in Chicago. If all goes to plan, Verlander will take the mound one last time.

“It’s been super frustrating because there’s been several setbacks along the way,” Verlander said. “And obviously if that happens now, then it’s no chance of me pitching. That’s why I think we’re being super cautious in saying, ‘Let’s get to the point where we know you can withstand the stress, and then just go. Have at it.’ There’s nothing to save at that point.”

When all is said and done, Verlander will retire with the three Cy Young Awards, two World Series championships, an ALCS MVP award, 10 All-Star selections, an AL MVP and Rookie of the Year, as well as over 3,000 strikeouts and 266 wins. He will be eligible for the Hall of Fame in 2031.

“It’s been very inspiring to hear the comments of how many fans just want to see me take the mound again,” he said. “It’s really cool to hear, and it means a lot to me.”

Cody Stavenhagen contributed to this report
